title: Card fill is indistinguishable from the panel it sits on
description:
Fallback capsule 0x282c33 against panel/bar background 0x1d2025 is 1.17:1. Monitor cards and bar pills share Theme.Capsule, mapped from Tokens.SurfaceContainer.

Two stories in the parity docs: the live DMS grim used widgetBackgroundColor "sch" (Material surface-container-high), but design D3 mapped the mid token SurfaceContainer. Fallback was then tuned to ~1.15:1 to match a measurement of that mid pairing. The contrast test floor is 1.10, which locks the problem in.

Raising Capsule globally would also change the bar. A panel-only step (map cards to surface-container-high, keep bar on SurfaceContainer) needs a second fill token; the matugen template currently emits only surface_container. Owner taste on which surface, not a missing paint path.

title: Two-up card grid needs a capsule to measure inside a row
description:
measureNode returned contentHeight as a capsule's height, which is right in the bar and wrong inside a column-nested row (columnChildHeight passed 1<<20). That is why the monitor panel could only stack full-width cards.

Fix is on branch fix/tier-2-panel-quality (5326a6d): the row case asks each child for its intrinsic height; a capsule with children honours an explicit Width so two cards share a row. Needs a live look of the monitor panel and of bar geometry before close. Not on main yet.

title: Two-up card grid needs a capsule to measure inside a row
description: The monitor panel stacks full-width cards; the reference lays them two to a row. measureNode returns contentHeight as a capsule's height, which is right in the bar where that is the band, and wrong inside a column-nested row where columnChildHeight passes 1<<20. A capsule in a row therefore measures to an absurd height and cannot be used for a grid cell. Either give the capsule an explicit height, or make its height its child plus padding and have the bar stretch it; the second changes freshly landed bar geometry and needs a live look.

title: M3: remove or make Metrics.Leased total
description: Metrics.Leased has no product callers; sampling uses SourceLeased. leaseSet is a value type, so a missing map key does not nil-deref. Dead export. Delete it unless a consumer appears. Not a live panic.

title: Group the sysmon widgets in one holder pill
description:
Live review 2026-08-31: cpu and memory each getting their own capsule reads as loose numbers. Owner wants them grouped; battery stays separate in its own pill.

The references disagree, so this is an owner decision, not a correction. DMS gives every status widget its own capsule. Noctalia runs the sysmon cluster as one continuous group with no inner pills.

Decision: one holder pill containing flat icon and value runs. Do not nest pills inside pills. The workspace row is already a pill row inside a capsule and reads as one indistinct blob in the live capture, our capsule contrast is 1.08 to 1 so two nested surfaces cannot be told apart, and Noctalia, the grouped reference, is flat inside.

Blocker: grouping is not expressible. Bar.Left, Center and Right are flat Item slices. Add an explicit group item carrying nested items, built as one capsule wrapping a KindRow. The layout machinery already exists from the parity tranche: capsuled wraps anything, measureNode sizes a row inside a capsule, and placeSection arranges capsule contents.

Sequence after sysc-53: a group of bare numbers is barely better than two pills of bare numbers, so the icons are what make a grouped cluster legible.

NOT RUN, needs a pointer or keyboard at the machine: right-click battery with left-click inert; hover and pressed state capture; Escape and outside-click closing; Super+X keybind (IPC equivalent was exercised instead). The shell IPC exposes only status, panel.toggle/open/close and osd.step, so it cannot synthesise pointer or key events.

NOT APPLICABLE on this hardware: battery card (desktop, no battery). Two-output case IS now runnable and the bar mapped on both outputs.

STILL OPEN from the plan: theme apply (valid light/dark, invalid, reduced motion) crossfade/retention/snap was not exercised live.

title: sysc-76 and sysc-125 are the same issue with one content hash
description:
Both records carry title "M6A Tasks 6-9 remain: attach plugin views to shell owners", the same description, the same created_at (2026-09-02 04:18) and the same content_hash 76f700ed. sysc-76 is in_progress with no dependencies; sysc-125 is closed and holds the depends-on edge to sysc-65. They are one issue that a past collision remap duplicated.

Consequence: any rebuild of beads.db from .beads/issues.jsonl silently drops one of them. 'bd import' reports "1 skipped" and the next 'bd sync --flush-only' writes a JSONL with 151 records instead of 152, so a commit made from a freshly built database commits the loss. This is how it surfaced: a worktree whose beads.db had to be recreated could not commit without dropping an issue.

Fix is to decide which record survives and delete or re-describe the other so the hashes differ. Whoever decides also settles whether M6A tasks 6-9 are done, since the two disagree on status.

title: Font shaper races under parallel shell tests
description:
go test -race ./internal/shell fails on main (cad5c92), independent of M7 wallpaper.

The race is inside go-text/typesetting font.go:664, reached through
internal/render/text.go:135 -> shell/bar.go:334 during layout. Parallel tests in
internal/shell share one shaper/font cache and measure concurrently;
TestBatteryPercentageReservesRoomForFullCharge is one reporter.

Found while executing docs/plans/2026-09-03-wallpaper.md Task 11, whose step 4
prescribes a race run over internal/shell. Recorded rather than worked around:
the wallpaper checks themselves pass, and internal/wallpaper is clean under -race.

Repro: GOMAXPROCS=4 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/shell

title: Wallpaper picker cannot reach a second library root
description:
D4's chrome calls for a folder strip (selector, not tiles). The M7 panel navigates
within the first library root only, so with the default two roots
(~/Pictures/Wallpapers and ~/Videos/Wallpapers) the video root is unreachable
from the picker.

Found by the 2026-09-04 live gate: the video had to be applied through the
engine directly. Recorded in tests/integration/README.md under Not covered here.

Fix: add the folder/root strip from D4 above the grid, listing each configured
root plus the current directory's children.

title: M7 wallpaper: picker chrome is a skeleton
description:
Shipped panel has the grid but not D4/D6/D7 controls: no title/close, no output
select, no All/Images/Videos filter, no Up, no folder strip, no Pause/Resume or
Restore buttons. The methods exist and are unit-tested; nothing invokes them
from the UI. Tiles also lack the current-assignment border, the missing-thumb
glyph, and the disabled-video treatment.

Also: gslapper maps a Background surface and reports playing while a competing
quickshell Background surface stays visible, so no wallpaper is actually shown
on this machine. D18 detection is unbuilt.

title: Static wallpaper fallback missing on the laptop
description: Neither awww nor swaybg is installed on archThink, so Restore has no static engine to hand off to and the picker's engine strip shows only the gSlapper pill. Fix is one command on that machine: sudo pacman -S swaybg. Recorded because the Restore path could not be exercised in the 2026-09-04 laptop gate.

title: Brightness control reports unavailable on hardware with a backlight
description: sysc-shell ipc osd.step {"kind":"brightness","action":"up"} returns "brightness unavailable" on archThink, which has /sys/class/backlight with a live value (24242). Audio on the same machine works after the wpctl suffix fix. Found while retiring the DMS keybinds: the brightness keys are the one pair with no working sysc-shell equivalent, so they were left pointing at dms. Start at services.Brightness.Available and how the device path is resolved.

title: Named colour-scheme palettes as a theme source
description:
appearance.source is wallpaper|hex|stock, defaulting to wallpaper, so the whole palette re-derives from whatever image is set. A user who wants a known scheme has no way to ask for one.

Add named palettes as a source alongside those three, following Noctalia's set: Ayu, Catppuccin, Dracula, Eldritch, Gruvbox, Kanagawa, Nord, Rose Pine, Tokyo Night, plus the shipped stock palette. Each is a complete 49-role Tokens table, so it goes through the same Valid/Repair contract as generated output rather than a second path.

Note appearance.scheme already exists but means the matugen algorithm variant (scheme-tonal-spot and friends), not a named palette. The two are different axes and both need to stay.
design: Palettes resolve to theme.Tokens and reuse the existing contrast validation. Noctalia caches downloaded palettes under ~/.local/state; a first cut can compile them in, since the fallback tables already establish that shape.
acceptance_criteria: A named palette can be selected and produces a complete validated palette in dark and light; wallpaper-derived theming still works unchanged; the setting is exposed alongside source/seed/scheme/mode.

title: External application theming, opt-in, with DMS parity
description:
sysc-shell writes no application theme files at all today. DankMaterialShell did, which is the parity gap: it wrote kitty, GTK, Qt and browser CSS from its palette.

Build that export, but opt-in per target rather than on by default. Nothing outside the shell should be rewritten because a wallpaper changed, unless the user asked for that target specifically. This came out of a real incident: DMS flipped isLightMode on a schedule and silently rewrote kitty to a light palette, and the cause took a long time to find precisely because the writes were invisible and unattributed.

Targets to cover for parity: kitty, GTK 3/4, Qt5ct/Qt6ct, terminal window borders, and browser CSS.
design: sysc-shell already writes ~/.cache/sysc-shell/colors.json, which is the same shape Noctalia uses as its export seam (~/.config/noctalia/colors.json plus user templates). Prefer templates over hardcoded per-app writers so a user can add a target without a code change. Each target needs an explicit enable, a recorded output path, and a way to see what was written.
acceptance_criteria: No file outside sysc-shell's own directories is written unless that target is explicitly enabled; enabling a target writes it and records where; disabling stops future writes and leaves the last output in place.
notes:
Correction after reading the tree: external application theming already EXISTS as internal/theming, and is already opt-in per target. It ships 16 templates (kitty, gtk3, gtk4, qt, alacritty, foot, ghostty, wezterm, niri, starship, btop, cava, emacs, helix, kcolorscheme, scroll) and settings exposes a theme.templates.<name> switch for each. An earlier note here said no export existed; that was wrong.

What was actually missing is now fixed under sysc-176 task 12: the template context exported 11 of the 49 roles from a hand-written list, so a template naming a secondary, an error container or any fixed accent silently rendered nothing, and Mode was pinned to dark. The context is built from the palette's own role table now, with mode and source metadata.

Remaining scope for this issue is therefore narrower than filed: audit the shipped templates against the full role set now that they can reach it, and compare the target list against what DankMaterialShell wrote (it also produced firefox and zen browser CSS, which have no template here).

title: Bar wallpaper widget is accepted by config but never built
description:
config.go knownItems contains "wallpaper" with a comment saying it opens the picker and is deliberately not in Default(), so a user adds it themselves. Adding it does validate. But widget.go buildWidgets has no case for it, so the item is silently dropped and no glyph appears on the bar.

The picker itself is complete: popout_wallpaper.go is implemented and parsePanelName maps "wallpaper" to PanelWallpaper, so it opens fine from a keybind or IPC. Only the bar affordance is missing.

Right-click is also unbound. bindBarPanelActionsLocked in registry.go binds buttonRight for monitor, session and notifications; there is no wallpaper arm, so nothing routes a button to the picker.
acceptance_criteria: A bar item with id wallpaper renders a glyph; clicking it toggles the wallpaper picker; right-click behaves consistently with the other panel widgets; an unknown item still fails loudly at load.

title: Tranche 4A implementation: panel foundation
description: 14 tasks in docs/plans/2026-08-30-panel-foundation.md. Blocked by the two review blockers, and by M2 corrections and tranche 3A per its own prerequisites.

title: Launcher browse list was capped at 50 entries
description:
The empty-query browse list arrived capped, so it stopped in the E's. sysc-launch's rank applies resultLimit=50 to every query; with an empty query every entry scores 0, the sort collapses to alphabetical, and the first 50 survive. Measured on the desktop: index 49 was 'Eye of GNOME', and 'Faugus' at index 50 was the first entry silently dropped. 199 visible entries were showing as 50.

Fixed in sysc-shell by injecting launcher.ServiceConfig.Rank (internal/shell/launcher_rank.go): the search cap is kept, the browse list is left whole. The ranker is a copy of the library's, pinned against the original by TestLauncherRankMatchesLibraryForSearches so search order cannot drift.

title: Held keys do not repeat: no client-side repeat timer
description:
wl_keyboard.repeat_info names a rate and delay once, and the compositor then sends exactly one key event per physical press; synthesising the rest is the client's job. niri never sends KeyboardKeyStateRepeated, and there was no repeat_info handler and no timer, so a held Down moved one row and a held Backspace deleted one character in every panel.

UPDATE 2026-09-06: implemented and landed in f755eea. The owner goroutine's poll deadline carries the repeat timer; repeatTimeout returns -1 when idle, fireRepeat delivers at most one synthetic press per pass, modifiers are exempt by evdev code, and repeat stops on release, on leave, and on capability loss. Unit tests in internal/platform/wayland/keyrepeat_test.go pass. Niri config confirms repeat-delay 600 / repeat-rate 25 so the path will engage.

STILL OPEN because it has not been confirmed with a real held keypress. wtype cannot be used to drive the panel: attaching a virtual keyboard drops the exclusive grab and dismisses it. Needs a human to hold Down in the launcher.

title: Launcher usage boost has no frequency signal past its caps
description:
Measured with a crafted history through the real ranker:

  boost= 25  used 200x today
  boost= 25  used  10x 5 days ago
  boost= 25  used 200x 5 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 40 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 40 days ago

Two flattenings. historyAmountCap=10 saturates the open count, then usageBoostCap=25 clamps the product, so anything opened a handful of times recently is indistinguishable. Then base = 10 - ageDays goes non-positive at 10 days and max(base*amount,1) collapses everything older to exactly 1: a daily driver used 200 times ranks level with something opened once last month, and the tie falls back to alphabetical.

The mechanism itself works -- 9 entries carry a boost on the desktop today and they do sort above the alphabetical run. This is the shape of the curve, not the wiring. Changing it is a behaviour change in sysc-launch, shared with its own consumers, so it needs agreement before shipping.

title: Stale wpctl step assertion in internal/shell/osd_test.go
description: ff1cd5d moved the wpctl relative-volume sign to a suffix ('5%+') and updated internal/services/audio_test.go, but internal/shell/osd_test.go kept asserting the old '+5%' prefix, so ./internal/shell was red on main. Production code is correct; the assertion was stale. Fixed as a one-line change while verifying the launcher work.

title: Running-apps bar pill
description:
One bar capsule of compact per-application icons for Niri UI windows. Design D1–D15 in docs/plans/2026-09-05-running-apps-pill-design.md; plan docs/plans/2026-09-05-running-apps-pill.md. Prior art docs/plans/2026-09-05-running-apps-pill-prior-art.md.

Default right, before cpu/memory. Left stays workspace + window-title. Left-click focus-or-cycle; right-click desktop Actions= plus Close all.

title: Theme system parity: semantic appearance, density, type, and motion
description: Owner requirement 2026-09-02. Approved design: docs/plans/2026-09-02-theme-system-parity-design.md. Executable plan: docs/plans/2026-09-02-theme-system-parity.md. Extend the existing native Go matugen/theme pipeline to DMS/Noctalia theme-system parity: a complete semantic palette, surface composition, independent density/type/shape/opacity/elevation/motion axes, bundled preset defaults, accessibility enforcement, settings, application-template export, and atomic live application. Depends on the completed chrome catalogue sysc-141.
notes:
Tasks 0-12 landed and checkpoint 2 passed on feature/theme-system-parity.

Automated gate green: gofmt clean, go vet ./... clean, go.mod/go.sum unchanged, git diff --check clean, worktree clean. All 33 packages pass -race individually, internal/shell 17.6s and tests/integration 36.8s included. The plan's 'go test -race ./...' was NOT run as written: that command hard-locks this machine (zram-only swap, 16-way linking) and a hook blocks it. Substituted per-package runs with GOMAXPROCS=2 -p 1.

Leftover inspection: no ProofStyle, no theme RGB in internal/shell or internal/ui, one animation ticker owner per surface. Remaining Bold: sites are all dynamic and legitimate -- notification body markup driven by the notification protocol, and tab/chip emphasis. Static 'Bold: true' is forbidden by a source-scan gate in internal/shell.

REMAINING: task 13's live Niri gate. It needs a human at the display: its ten configurations are verified by confirming text does not clip, hit targets stay aligned, and cards separate. Cannot be completed autonomously.

Notable defects found and fixed along the way, none of which were in the plan:
- go test ./internal/shell ran loginctl terminate-session self for real, killing the developer's SSH session on a green run.
- Every popout resolved ThemeFromTokens(tokens, 12), rebuilding the default composition, so only the palette ever reached a panel. Density, radius, font scale and preset stopped at the bar.
- surfaceTheme had the same defect, so a reload carried a palette change to open surfaces and nothing else.

title: Running-apps and tray dropdowns hang below the clicked icon
description: Live: Steam (running-apps) and other tray item menus appear at the right of the output, not under the icon. runningAppMenuHost.spec() anchors Top|Right. Tray already has trayMenuUnderBar(anchor) with bar-node output coordinates; running-apps must reuse it with the tile Bounds (running-app:<key>). Empty Rect must not fall back to the output origin or the right edge.
acceptance_criteria: Right-click Steam or a tray item: the overlay left edge aligns with the icon and the top edge is just below the bar/icon. Spec is Top|Left plus margins from trayMenuUnderBar, not Top|Right. Named test asserts those margins from a known tile Rect.

title: Running-apps overlay is stuck: rows unselectable, no dismiss, eats bar clicks
description: Live: menu items cannot be chosen; no way to exit; overlay stays up and intercepts left-clicks. Host uses keyboardOnDemand so Escape never arrives; handle only EventPointerRelease (no press pairing); 280px Top|Right overlay covers tray and tiles. Need Exclusive keyboard, Escape closes, press+release on rows, click-outside (panel shieldSpec pattern or miss), second right-click toggles (close then open already exists).
acceptance_criteria: Escape, click outside, and choosing a row all close the overlay. After close, bar left-clicks reach running-app tiles again. Rows accept press+release. Overlay no longer covers the tray because placement is under the icon (sysc placement bug).

title: Running-apps menu rows have no gap and paint a solid accent blob
description: Live: strange blue element below the tray / first menu row. rebuild() is KindColumn Gap 0; cursor row FillAccent; KindButton height 28. Tray/panel use Gap 6-8 and FillSoft hover wash. Do not FillAccent row 0 by default — that is the blue stadium under the tray when the overlay is Top|Right.
acceptance_criteria: Visible gap between rows. Hover/cursor uses FillSoft (or equivalent wash), not a solid accent pill on the first row. Named paint/layout check for Gap > 0.

title: M4 parallel prework: panel model and rendering
description: Execute Tranche 4A Tasks 1, 5, and 8 while Tranche 3A continues. Task 3 may start after the matugen external-binary decision closes. Do not touch M3-owned config, registry, bar, Wayland client, UI tree, or process wiring until sysc-6 merges.

title: Running-apps focus chrome is a tiny stadium behind the icon
description: Live: focused-app highlight is a small pill behind the icon, not around it. FillAccent on a 24x24 KindCapsule with no Radius paints a stadium; 18px icon sits on top and accent peeks as a sliver. KindCapsule measure also ignores Height so the tile can stretch to bar height. Need an explicit Radius (rounded square chip) that wraps the whole icon; FillSoft wash is acceptable if the whole tile reads as selected.
acceptance_criteria: Focused tile chrome surrounds the entire icon, not a sliver behind it. Explicit Radius so it is not a circle-stadium. Measure respects Height: runningAppTile so the chip is 24x24 (or the chosen tile size) centred in the bar.

title: Running-apps and tray icons lose resolution at bar size
description: Live: compact bar icons look soft. attachRunningIconsLocked requests Square(name, size) at 18 if bar.scale120() is 0 and never re-requests after configure. decodeRaster uses ApproxBiLinear; paintImage is nearest-neighbour and upscales if the raster is smaller than the box. Shared one Image for all bars. Do not start a second icon worker; reuse trayIcons. Request at Physical size after configure.
acceptance_criteria: Icons requested at Physical(runningAppIconSize) once scale is known; a configure that changes scale re-requests. Raster edge matches the paint box so paintImage does not upscale. Tray path already uses trayIconPixelSize — keep that, do not regress it.

title: Running-apps left-click focus-or-cycle does not fire on the live bar
description: Live: left click on a running-app tile does nothing. handleRunningAppClick + nextFocusID + sendNiriLocked(FocusWindow) exist and pass table tests. Likely the stuck overlay eating pointer, and/or tiles not hit-testing (outer capsule has no Action; inner tiles have running-app:<key>). Re-check after overlay placement and dismiss; if hit-test is also wrong, fix Hit/Action on the tile once.
acceptance_criteria: With no overlay open, left click focuses the app if unfocused and cycles to the next window if already focused. Works on the live bar, not only in TestRunningAppsClick.

title: Panel corners composite as black: opaque region ignores the radius
description:
Every panel in the shell claimed its whole rectangle was opaque, including the rounded corners.

internal/platform/wayland/aux.go applyAuxRegions passed a hardcoded radius of 0 to applyOpaqueRegion. With radius 0, opaqueRects returns the full body rect, so the compositor was told it could skip blending the corners. The painter meanwhile does clear(c.Pix) and fills a *rounded* body, so those corner pixels are genuinely transparent -- composited unblended they come out pure black behind the border.

Measured on the desktop at the launcher panel's top-left corner arc:
  before: 32 of 78 pixels pure #000000
  after :  0 of 78, every corner pixel identical to the desktop behind it

The bar was never affected: applyHostRegions already passes policy.Radius. Theme.Radius's own doc comment says it 'rounds the body's corners and shapes the opaque region' -- the aux path just never received it.

Fixed by adding HostCallbacks.Radius, set from h.theme.Radius in panelSpec, and using it in both applyAuxRegions branches. Surfaces that do not set OpaqueBackground get no opaque region at all and were never affected. Regression test: TestPanelSurfaceCarriesItsCornerRadius.

title: Theme system parity: semantic appearance, density, type, and motion
description: Owner requirement 2026-09-02. Approved design: docs/plans/2026-09-02-theme-system-parity-design.md. Executable plan: docs/plans/2026-09-02-theme-system-parity.md. Extend the existing native Go matugen/theme pipeline to DMS/Noctalia theme-system parity: a complete semantic palette, surface composition, independent density/type/shape/opacity/elevation/motion axes, bundled preset defaults, accessibility enforcement, settings, application-template export, and atomic live application. Depends on the completed chrome catalogue sysc-141.

title: Launcher SYSC rail and DMS panel height
description:
Plate A's shape plus the approved header, live on the desktop.

The rail is //////SYSC////// -- six slashes each side in RoleTitle and the new ToneAccent, with the real brand mark between them as KindWordmark. The mark is an embedded alpha master (internal/render/icons/wordmark/, from sysc-greet assets/logo.png at ccfcdde) scaled with CatmullRom and blended with the accent, so it re-colours with the theme instead of pinning a brand colour into a wallpaper-derived palette.

Panel 500 -> 700, DMS spotlight's own height. Visible rows 6.2 -> 8.5. Search field 44 -> 56.

New primitives, all with tests:
  ui.KindWordmark  -- a wide tinted mark; KindIcon reserves a square
  ui.Node.CenterX  -- centres a column child by narrowing its track to the
                      child's measured width, so a container centres with its
                      contents rather than laying out across the full width
  ui.ToneAccent    -- accent-coloured text
  render.Wordmark  -- cached alpha masks per physical size

The three copies of the list-viewport arithmetic are now one launcherListHeight, and the chrome above it is measured rather than assumed: a constant header height was 5px out from what the row laid out and left a dead strip along the panel floor. TestLauncherListReachesThePanelFloor pins it.

Still open from the audit: hover state on rows, the footer help line, DMS's 12/16 row spacing, and the clear button in the field.

title: Startup errors are swallowed: deferred registry.Close deadlocks
description:
Any error returned by run() presents as a silent hang with no message, because the deferred registry.Close() at cmd/sysc-shell/main.go:77 blocks forever on r.mu.Lock() at internal/shell/registry.go:725. A goroutine dump taken during the hang shows goroutine 1 parked in Close via deferreturn and no other goroutine holding the mutex, so the lock was leaked on a path that returned while holding it.

Found while diagnosing the wallpaper-widget nil deref (sysc-169). That panic surfaced as 'wayland: second roundtrip: dispatch: panic handling opcode=2 senderID=4: nil pointer dereference' -- but the message never reached the journal, and the shell just sat in futex_do_wait with no Wayland connection, no IPC listener and no bar. It was only recoverable by temporarily converting run() to a named return and logging before Close.

Fixing sysc-169 removed today's trigger; this hides the next one.

Repro: make run() return any error after the registry is constructed, then start the shell. Observe a hang instead of the error.

title: Audit running-apps pill implementation against design, prior art, and owner live feedback
description:
Post-implementation audit of the 2026-09-05 running-apps bar pill session. Commission: docs/plans/2026-09-06-running-apps-pill-audit-handover.md. Compare landed code (and the uncommitted sysc-181 working tree) to D1-D15, the prior-art note, plan Task 9 live gate, and the owner's live UI feedback. Write docs/plans/2026-09-06-running-apps-pill-audit-report.md. Scoped tests only.

UPDATE 2026-09-06: the working-tree diff this audit was commissioned against is now committed as 88ac06c (code) and 6f69bf6 (handover, register row, D10 amendment). It was left uncommitted behind sysc-181, which was already closed, so it was one stray checkout away from being lost. Audit 88ac06c rather than a working tree; the content is identical, verified against the preserved copy on branch backup/sysc-181-wip (886da73).

Tests green at the merge point across shell, ui, render, icons, niri and wayland.
acceptance_criteria: One audit-report on main docs/plans with Blocking/Significant/Minor findings, a proceed or corrections or redesign verdict, and a beads note on whether sysc-175 and sysc-182 should stay open. Register the report in docs/plans/README.md.

title: sysc-metrics M2: power and thermal collectors
description: Unbuilt and undesigned upstream work that gates Tranche 3C. Filed in the repo itself as https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-metrics/issues/1 so it is visible to whoever picks that module up. External repo /home/nomadx/sysc-metrics at v0.1.0: no Go file mentions battery, thermal, upower or power_supply. Its design specifies the contract: thermal-zone parsing, UPower DisplayDevice preferred, sysfs power-supply fallback, source-transition handling, multi-battery, and suspend/resume qualification on real hardware. Tranche 3C's design assumes a provisional BatterySnapshot shape recorded in that issue; a divergence triggers a reconciliation pass rather than a redesign. Needs its own design and plan there, then a v0.2.0 release tag.

title: Launcher rows render at half height for some entries
description:
Reported 2026-09-06. In the launcher result list most rows draw at the full 60px slot, but some entries draw at roughly half that. Confirmed by eye on pwvucontrol, sonusmix, rofi, and rofi theme selector; there are likely more.

The list is a KindVirtualList with a fixed ItemHeight of launcherSlotHeight, so every slot is the same size by construction. That means the row content, not the slot, is short: launcherRow builds a capsule per result and something about these particular entries is producing a shorter subtree.

First thing to check is what these .desktop files have in common that the others do not, since they are all recently installed and several are Rofi related. Candidates: a missing Comment so the row has one text line instead of two, a missing or unresolvable Icon so the capsule loses the 40px icon slot that sets the row's floor, or a NoDisplay/OnlyShowIn field changing the shape of the entry.

Verify against the real desktop files in /usr/share/applications before changing layout code.

title: Launcher search field: glyph, border, tokens, and text baseline
description:
Design audit raised 2026-09-06, against the Noctalia launcher as reference.

Four defects in one control, all in paintTextField:

1. Typed text sits against the top edge of the well instead of on its midline. paintText draws from the top of the box it is given; invisible while a field was only as tall as its text, obvious now the field is a 56px pill.
2. The magnifier was built from a filled square with a smaller square punched out in the well colour, plus a staircase of 3x3 blocks for the handle. It cannot antialias, and the punch-out assumes a flat well behind it. It also sat 13px from the left edge, inside the curve of the stadium cap, so it read as crowding the corner.
3. The border did not render crisply. It was drawn as a fill of the border colour with a smaller fill laid on top, so the border was the arithmetic difference of two silhouettes quantised to whole pixels, which thins and breaks up around the corners. The same construction was used for the panel's own rim.
4. The field stroked Rim, which is the floating panel's edge token. The field and the panel it sits on drew the same colour, so neither read as deliberate. A field is a control and should carry Outline.

WORK IN PROGRESS on feature/launcher-ui-parity: added RingMask and SearchGlyphMask as antialiased cached masks, routed strokeRoundedRect and the panel rim through the ring, moved the field to Outline, gave the focused field the existing 2px accent focus ring, and added centreLine. Four render tests still need updating to the new geometry.

title: Launcher panel: shadow instead of a drawn rim
description:
Raised 2026-09-06. The launcher currently separates itself from the wallpaper with a 1px rim. The reference (Noctalia) draws no outline at all and relies on a soft shadow.

This is not a paint-only change. panelhost sets style.Body to the full logical surface, so the painted body fills the layer surface edge to edge and a shadow has nowhere to go: it would be clipped at the surface boundary.

Doing it properly means giving the panel surface a transparent margin and insetting the body by the shadow spread, which touches panel sizing, the body rect, the input region, and the opaque region (which must cover only the body, or the compositor will composite the margin as opaque and reintroduce the black corners fixed in sysc-183).

The renderer already has what it needs: Canvas.DrawShadow, ShadowTexture, and theme Elevation/Shadow tokens, currently used only by menus.

Estimate is small but cross-cutting, and it affects every panel, so it wants its own slice rather than being folded into the search field work.

title: Launcher chrome remainder from the plate A design pass
description:
Raised across 2026-09-05/06. Items from the approved plate A design that the rail, panel height, hints and browse-list work did not cover:

HANDOVER 2026-09-06: docs/plans/2026-09-06-launcher-chrome-remainder-handover.md commissions the remaining three items for a fresh session. Item 3, the rail slash weight, is an owner decision and must be put to them with two rendered options rather than chosen.

comments.author: nomadx
comments.text:
Landed on branch feature/launcher-chrome-remainder (19a4ea6, 77d3b99, 207f9e1),
worktree at ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/sysc-shell/feature/launcher-chrome-remainder.
Not merged to main.

1. Row spacing -- done. The row capsule now stands launcherRowHeight 68 with
   launcherRowPadTop 12 and launcherRowPadBottom 16 around a 40px glyph. A ui
   node has one padding scalar, so the capsule takes the top figure and a
   column inside it spends the 4px difference at the foot; a row in that box
   would centre its children and split it. The slot went 68 -> 76.

   Cost: the 700-tall panel now shows 7 whole rows and a partial, not 8.
   TestLauncherListFillsThePanel's floor moved 8 -> 7 with the reason recorded
   in the test. TestLauncherListReachesThePanelFloor is untouched and green --

title: Wallpaper picker: let the engine strip choose an engine, not just report one
description:
Raised by the owner 2026-09-06 on the reworked picker: 'there is no default selected.. also clicking on one of the engines does not highlight the button, there is also no hover over effect like with the other buttons'.

The default half is fixed (2885264): Capabilities.EngineFor is now the single statement of which engine an apply uses, the store records it per output in Runtime.Engine, and an output nothing has painted yet reports the engine that would take it, so a pill is always marked.

The clicking half is not, and cannot be without new plumbing. There is no engine override anywhere: gslapperEngine.Apply picks gSlapper whenever caps.GSlapper is set and the static fallback otherwise, and Service.set is fixed at construction, so nothing can express 'use swaybg on DP-1'. Making the pills clickable today would be a control that highlights and changes nothing.

Work, if taken:
- wallpaper.Settings gains an engine preference, honoured by Apply, with the hard constraint that a video can only be gSlapper and a pill for an engine that cannot serve the current assignment must be disabled rather than silently ignored.
- The service needs a way to take new Settings after construction (a Command op), since it currently only ever reads the ones it was built with.
- config.Wallpaper gains the field, with load validation, the write diff, and defaults, so the choice survives a restart like every other picker choice.
- Only then do the pills get Action and Focusable, at which point they pick up hover and press from interaction.apply for free.

Until then the strip is deliberately a readout: Role status, no Action, no Focusable.
acceptance_criteria: An engine chosen in the picker paints the next apply on that output, survives a restart, and a pill that cannot serve the current assignment is visibly disabled rather than inert.

title: setSessionProfile runs a command under Registry.mu
description:
internal/shell/popout_session.go:243 calls r.runArgv(powerProfileSetArgv(name)) straight from an action handler, which holds Registry.mu. That is command I/O under the lock, which the project constraint forbids: no command or filesystem work may run while Registry.mu or the Wayland owner is blocked.

The same file already has the correct shape two functions up: scheduleLoadProfiles copies the exec hooks, runs off the owner without the lock, re-takes it, checks the panel host is still current, then applies. The set path should schedule the same way.

Found while designing the control centre (sysc-158). The control centre routes every command through its own scheduleControl seam rather than copying this, so it is not blocked on the fix.

CPU/power case, evidence found 2026-09-13 while scoping the idle run (the run itself is deferred):

archPC's journal records one sysc-shell run consuming 10h 11min 23s of CPU over 23h 2min 8s wall clock, logged at 2026-09-13T14:21:18, so covering roughly 2026-09-12 15:18 to 2026-09-13 14:21. That is about 44 percent of one core sustained for a day. Other long runs on the same era of binary sat far lower: 45min 24s over 22h 38min (3.3 percent) and 44min 26s over 1d 2h 49min (2.8 percent), and 1h 56min over 22h 40min (8.6 percent). The spread matters more than any single figure: something makes this shell burn a core intermittently, and that is exactly the failing case this epic names.

Not yet attributable to a commit. The binary deployed on archPC at the time was a foreign build (mod 77a66f10ce75+dirty, zero screencopy symbols), not the blur or smoothness work.

Measured on this machine 2026-09-12 (go1.27.0, powersave governor, Ryzen 7 5700X, Audio region 1120x960): blur kernel 4.94 ms median against a predicted 4.60, linear at 4.6-5.1 ms/MPix across six panel sizes; screencopy readback 5.67 ms median against the 15 ms stop threshold in D16.1; about 11 ms per open, inside one 60 Hz frame.

Design corrections found live: this Niri offers xrgb8888 only for a region capture, so the captured alpha byte must be filled; a screencopy target's pool must hold exactly one buffer, which newGeneration cannot do; the backdrop must be clipped to the rounded mask or panel corners fill in; and the shell, not the wayland package, assembles the Style for panels, so the image returns through a new HostCallbacks.Backdrop. Ships off by default. The live gate is tracked separately.

title: Panel backdrop blur: screencopy binding and blur kernel
description:

Measured 2026-09-12/13 (go1.27.0, Ryzen 7 5700X, powersave): blur kernel 4.94 ms median against a predicted 4.60, linear at 4.6-5.1 ms/MPix over six panel sizes; screencopy readback 5.67 ms median against D16.1's 15 ms stop threshold; ~11 ms per open, inside one 60 Hz frame.

Design corrections found live, each by measurement rather than reading: this Niri offers xrgb8888 only for a region capture, so the captured alpha byte must be filled; a screencopy target's wl_shm pool must hold exactly one buffer, which newGeneration cannot do (hence newCaptureBuffer); the backdrop must go through the rounded mask or panel corners fill in; the shell, not the wayland package, assembles a panel's Style, so the image returns via a new HostCallbacks.Backdrop; and the panel-opacity bound had to move in three places or the lower floor stayed unreachable from config.

capture_output_region is OUTPUT-RELATIVE, not global: probed directly because this output sits at logical 2560,0. A global-space region is refused with nil, an output-relative one returns real content. D3 assumed this and never verified it.

Post-rebase defect found and fixed (876ca72): main's AttachedPanelStyle resolves an attached panel's root at the BAR's opacity, which is opaque, so an attached panel painted straight over its own backdrop. Caught by measuring a live capture: the Audio panel body was a single flat colour, pixel-identical to the bar fill. rootStyle now keeps the panel's own alpha whenever a backdrop is present, with a regression test.

Verified live on two machines: archPC 3440x1440 scale 1.0 and archThink 1920x1080 scale 1.25 (the first fractional-scale exercise of this path). Blur visible on both; ships off by default.

title: Weather surfaces are unstyled and under-informed: audit and parity pass
description:
Audit 2026-09-15 of every first-party weather presentation against the DMS/Noctalia v4 reference (docs/plans/assets/2026-08-31-bar-visual-parity/refs/noctalia-weather.png).

Presentations today, three sites, all thin:

- Bar widget (widget.go:226, weatherwidget.go): one text run - inline WMO glyph + temperature + optional condition word + stale age. The glyph is text, not an icon node: it inherits text tone and metrics, so sysc-58's advance defect applies to it. The tooltip is the static word "Weather" (textWidget.tooltip is a plain string). No Action is set: clicking does nothing.
- Control centre weather page (controlcenter_pages.go:349 ccWeather): a Today card that presents raw coordinates ("%.2f deg, %.2f deg") as the location plus "Updated 15:04"; below it four 143x132 forecast cards showing day name, glyph and "H / L" only - no condition word, today excluded, count pinned at four.
- No standalone weather panel exists.

Data path (weather/client.go, weather/model.go, internal/services/weather.go): the request carries current=temperature_2m,weather_code and daily=weather_code,max,min,sunrise,sunset for seven days. Open-Meteo also returns, and Decode silently discards, elevation and timezone from the response root; the current block can carry is_day, apparent_temperature, humidity, wind_speed_10m, wind_direction_10m and uv_index; the daily block can carry uv_index_max and precipitation figures. The reference panel shows wind, UV, elevation and a named timezone; none of that is reachable today without extending the wire model.

Vocabulary drift - three copies of the same facts:

- Icon mapping: render/iconfont.go IconRune/IconName (eight WMO glyphs) versus ccWeatherIcon's separate Material ligature set (sunny, partly_cloudy_day, ...) for the same codes.
- Condition words: conditionWords (weatherwidget.go:14), ccWeatherCondition, and the plugin's Condition() are three tables. The plugin's routes through IconName; the shell's two do not agree with each other.
- No night variants: WMO code 0 at night renders a sun; is_day is not fetched.

State handling drift: formatWeather's three-state rule (placeholder / error / stale-with-age) lives in the bar only. ccWeather dashes and "Updated HH:MM" ignore FailedSince, so an aged reading renders identically to a fresh one.

Conformance and collision hazards: ccWeather's geometry (Height 336/480, 132; Width 143; Gap 8/12) sits on the open token-conformance worklist, and the parked feature/noctalia-parity session has controlcenter_pages.go dirty in its worktree. This slice must not re-edit that page's geometry concurrently - sequence the cc page after parity lands or confine this slice to new files.
acceptance_criteria:
- weather.Query/Forecast/Decode extended for current is_day, apparent_temperature, wind speed and direction, humidity, uv_index; daily uv_index_max and precipitation; root elevation, timezone, timezone_abbreviation. Decode stays strict: checked pointer fields, bounded body, table tests for the new fields.
- One icon mapping and one condition-word table shared by the bar, the control-centre page and the tooltip; night variants for clear and partly-cloudy added to the icon subset and selected via is_day.
- The bar weather widget renders a real icon node beside the temperature, opens the weather panel as its Action, and its tooltip carries current facts rather than the literal word "Weather".
- A standalone PanelWeather appended to the PanelID enum after PanelNetwork (the blur coverage walk must see it), composed like the reference: hero card (large glyph, temperature, min/max, condition, configured location name - not coordinates), a details card (feels-like, wind, humidity, UV, sunrise, sunset, elevation, timezone), and the seven-day list with per-day icon, day, range and condition word. Daily only; Hourly is a separate decision with its own wire growth.
- Stale and error states follow formatWeather's three-state rule on every surface; an aged reading looks aged everywhere.
- No new literal geometry: spacing from the margin ladder, control sizes from the density row, shapes from the shape role. The control-centre page's existing literals stay untouched until the parity conversion lands.
- Focused checks per changed unit; gofmt, go vet, and the affected-package gates pass before any commit.

The hourly presentation is intentionally capped at seven rows to match the reference; the panel remains two-column per the recorded amendment; the city-only unresolved fallback retains the configured city label rather than fabricating zero coordinates.

title: Notification cards pad from a package constant, not the density row

Reconciling it is a measured-geometry change, not a constant swap: innerW := surfaceW - 4*cardPadding sizes the filter row, and the comment there records that widening that box squeezes 'Yesterday (N)' out of its slot and the compositor tears the panel down. title: Control centre quick tiles pad on the panel rung, not the card rung
description: ccQuickTile (controlcenter_pages.go:314) and ccBatteryTile (:332) set Padding: theme.MarginL (13). MarginL is the PanelPadding rung; the density row's CardPadding is 9 (MarginM). Three of the control centre's eight cards therefore do not read the card rung, surfaced when parity Task 10 widened TestSurfaceCardPaddingFollowsDensity to every openable panel. Changing it moves measured geometry: the tiles are a fixed ccCardH=88 inside a composition sized to fill its container exactly, and the handover records that an overflow there makes configure() refuse the child. title: Host-owned animated weather effects
description: Execute docs/plans/2026-09-16-effect-rendering.md: add the validated KindEffect retained-tree layer, bounded deterministic weather rasterizer, stack painting and clipping, existing animator phase lifecycle, standalone and Control Centre weather consumers, safety gates, and the owner-gated laptop Niri completion handover. acceptance_criteria: Focused UI/render/shell tests, race/vet/format/module gates, deterministic bounded weather pixels, reduced-motion behavior, both target surfaces animated, plugin boundary unchanged, and laptop Niri lifecycle records no leaked surface.

title: Bar clips overflowing right-side items silently instead of degrading gracefully
description:
When the right side of the bar holds more items than fit the output width, the shell silently clips whatever lands past the screen edge: with four plugin widgets plus the existing group, battery, volume, wifi, notifications, and media, the timer label was cut mid-glyph and battery through media vanished entirely. Found live on the laptop while verifying the sysc-plugins rebuild (2026-09-16, 1920-wide output).

Reproduce: place enough right-side items to exceed the width (four plugin placements is enough at 1920) and look at the right edge.

Expected: items that do not fit collapse (hide-when-tight behaviour like other shells), move to an overflow slot, or the bar refuses the placement at config load with a diagnostic -- anything but silent clipping. Config load already validates placements; the overflow case needs the same treatment at layout time.
notes: Owned by M9 sub-project C as of 2026-09-17: sysc-322 subsumes this. docs/plans/2026-09-17-bar-geometry-design.md D4 takes overflow because what does not fit is axis-dependent, so it is solved once for all four bar edges rather than fixed horizontally and reopened when the bar turns vertical. D5 is the policy: whole items drop in declaration order from the section's far end behind a visible indicator whose own extent is reserved before selection. Explicitly not refusal at config load, which this issue already rules out because plugin widgets appear and disappear at runtime. Do not fix separately in ui.ArrangeBar; that function is gated on sysc-314.

title: M10 centre composition: clock, media, fixed wordmark
description: Execute docs/plans/2026-09-16-centre-clock-media-wordmark-design.md. Make the default time/date one visible composition, keep media optional at its right edge, and anchor the SYSC wordmark at the bar content-band centre as widths and player state change.
design: Use the existing clock, media, wordmark, retained-tree, and ArrangeBar seams. Add no general layout toolkit or new media protocol. Keep all service work off Registry.mu and the Wayland dispatch loop.
acceptance_criteria: Focused build and layout tests prove one time/date group, media collapse and bounded title behavior, stable accessible actions, and an invariant wordmark centre across side-width and media variations. A DP-1 bare-metal bar check records no leaked or drifting composition.

title: M10 notifications and battery warning
description: Execute docs/plans/2026-09-16-notifications-battery-urgency-design.md. Give low, normal, and critical cards semantic urgency treatment and integrate one hysteretic, deduplicated battery warning through a qualified sysc-notify producer.
design: sysc-notify remains the record and FDO publisher. The shell consumes the shared battery snapshot and sends a bounded replacement-key command only through the qualified producer; no local notification database or fake success.
acceptance_criteria: Focused shell tests prove all urgency roles, critical accessibility treatment, stable unread geometry, and battery enter/hold/recovery, reconnect, invalid-input, and producer-failure behavior. The sysc-notify producer protocol and daemon tests pass before the shell pin changes; the live gate does not spam notification history or invent a battery reading.
notes: Implemented in sysc-notify 92a3f9c/v0.1.0-rc.4 and sysc-shell 410e4a6. Service vet and all package race tests pass; shell feature race tests and full notifyclient/shell non-race tests pass. Full shell race still hits the pre-existing Bluetooth/media-relay race and publishMediaSnapshot nil panic.

title: M10 tray termination and external qualification
description: Execute docs/plans/2026-09-16-owned-tray-termination-design.md. Define, test, tag, and pin the sysc-tray owned termination operation, then add the shell Close row and acknowledgement path.
design: Ownership, PID/start-time validation, lifecycle authority, and process operations stay in sysc-tray. sysc-shell adds no os.Kill, PID parsing, hidden-only removal, or arbitrary process signalling.
acceptance_criteria: sysc-tray protocol and daemon tests reject unsupported, stale, recycled, cross-UID, and busy identities; accept only a same-UID current owned item; request bounded graceful termination; and publish the matching item delta. Shell tests send only the full ItemKey, keep the row visible on rejection or timeout, and report success only after removal. A disposable fixture or an explicit unrun live gate is recorded without touching unrelated tray applications.
notes: Evidence 2026-09-25: sysc-tray v0.1.0-rc.3 protocol, ownership, app-rejection, and terminate integration tests pass (protocol and ownership packages; private-D-Bus TestTerminateRejectsUnknownKeys/UnestablishedIdentity and TestTerminateClosesARegisteredItem/TimesOutOnAStubbornProcess). sysc-shell Close-path tests pass for full ItemKey dispatch, pending state, rejection, disconnect, and settling only on matching removal. Live shell tray fixture intentionally unrun; no unrelated tray app was touched. This satisfies the acceptance alternative to record the unrun live fixture.

title: Settings rows overflow the panel's right edge
description:
On a 1536x864 logical output at scale 1.25 the settings pane clips every trailing control at the right edge: the enum pills (wallpaper, catppuccin, dark, standard, mini) are cut mid-word and the appearance.seed field runs past the viewport. Reproduced live on the laptop, twice, with screenshots.

Giving the scroll column an explicit width (panel - 2*PanelPadding - rail - MarginXL), mirroring ccBodyWidth, improved it but did not close it, so a row is still measuring wider than the column. The likely cause is the label column: Entry.Describe renders as a single unwrapped text node, so a long description forces the row wide and pushes the right-pinned control past the edge. Wrapping the caption to the label column's available width is the thing to check first.

Not visible on a 3440x1440 output at scale 1.0, which is why the per-package tests and the first live gate both passed. Found by M9 sub-project A's live check on a second machine.

title: Plugin cards do not use the settings row anatomy
description:
The Plugins section renders the plugin host's own composition: a meta line, an enable switch, a Retry button, then per-setting rows. Since M9 sub-project A the rest of the pane is label over caption with a right-pinned control and a reset that appears only on a changed row, so the section reads as a different product.

Bounding the column stopped the switches stretching the whole surface (done in A), but it did not make the cards read like settings. The work is in internal/shell/popout_plugins.go and pluginSettingRow rather than the settings pane, and it needs a decision about how much of Entry's anatomy a plugin-declared setting can borrow: a plugin manifest declares a label and a type but no description or default, so IsDefault and the caption line have no source unless the manifest grows one.

Flagged by the owner on the laptop during the A live check.

title: M3: render tooltips from the accepted theme and font
description: Tooltip paint hardcodes size, radius, background, foreground, and default font instead of the accepted configuration. The 3D completion handover already records this defect; resolve it through the current theme/font owner without adding a second theme model.

title: Settings font picker is not searchable
description:
D8 of docs/plans/2026-09-15-settings-foundation-design.md ships a searchable picker in the control vocabulary. Sub-project A built the enumerating half only: settingsFontFamilies reads fontscan.SystemFonts, dedupes and sorts, then hands the list to the ordinary Menu. This workstation has 720 families, so the control is a wall rather than a picker.

Approach that fits the existing machinery: Menu gains an optional retained ui.Field rendered as the first child of the open popup and named so PanelHost.editField can route IME to it, the way Search and Password already are. Menu.Next, Menu.Prev and Menu.PickAt then move over the filtered indices while index and cursor stay indices into the full option list, so Select commits the right value and PickAt accounts for the field occupying the first child slot. Opening the menu focuses the field.

Reached by internal/shell/popout_settings.go settingsMenuControl and internal/shell/menu.go.

title: Weather unit and interval are silently dropped when weather is unconfigured
description:
config.Write only emits a weather block when Weather.Configured is true. The settings entries for weather.unit and weather.interval set neither the value's flag nor Configured, so changing the unit on a weather that has never been given a place writes nothing: the pane shows the new value, the file does not carry it, and the next load returns the old one. Setting a place sets the flag, which is why this is invisible once a location exists.

This needs a decision rather than a patch. Having unit set Configured pins the location to 0,0, which is worse than dropping the write. Candidates: emit the weather block whenever any weather field departs from Default(), which makes Configured a derived property of the block rather than a flag; or keep the flag and have the pane disable or annotate unit and interval until a place is set, so the control is honestly unavailable rather than quietly ineffective.

Found during M9 sub-project A. internal/config/write.go and the weather entries in internal/settings/registry.go.

title: Font families are shown in their normalized form
description:
The picker lists dejavusans rather than DejaVu Sans. fontscan stores Footprint.Family normalized, and D10 of the settings foundation design allowed presenting normalized names explicitly, calling a display form its own decision. It still looks wrong in the pane.

The decision is what the display form is derived from, because the normalized string is lossy and title-casing it does not recover word boundaries. The honest source is the font file's own name table rather than the footprint. Worth settling alongside the searchable picker, since both change the same control.

title: A described settings row measures itself instead of taking a ladder height
description:
Every other settings row takes Metrics.StandardControl. A row with a description is two stacked lines and a fixed height cropped the caption, so settingsEntryRow sets Height only when Describe is empty. The density ladder therefore governs the text inside a described row but not the row box, which is not what the design says.

Closing it properly means a minimum height rather than a fixed one, and internal/ui carries no MinHeight on Node today. That is a layout-engine addition with reach beyond this pane, so it wants a decision before it is made: either add MinHeight and have every settings row take the ladder as a floor, or amend the design to say that a described row is self-measuring. internal/shell/popout_settings.go settingsEntryRow.

title: Plugin setting rows do not use the settings pane's row anatomy
description:
The Plugins section renders the plugin host's own composition: a meta line, a switch, a Retry button, then per-setting rows. Sub-project A bounded that column so it stopped stretching the surface, but it still does not read like settings next to the label-over-caption rows every other section now uses.

Flagged by the owner during A and deliberately left, because the change is to internal/shell/popout_plugins.go and pluginSettingRow rather than to the settings pane. It carries its own decision: how much of settings.Entry's anatomy a plugin-declared setting can borrow, given a plugin declares a label and a type but no description or group.

title: Home System card: four 40px radial gauges in one row
description:
Owner-approved 2026-09-17. Design package: docs/plans/assets/2026-09-17-metrics-control-centre-radial-design/.

Replace the provisional 22px two-row layout, which overflows the padded System card by 4px at font scale 100, 13px at 125, 29px at 150, and fails to lay out at 200.

Composition: four 40px rings in one row, value centred inside each ring, caption beneath, no card title. Content 57 of the 70px interior.

Approved amendments (design.md D2):
1. Drop the 'System' card title; keep an accessible group name on the card.
2. Visible caption 'Temp'; accessible name 'CPU temperature'.
3. paintRadialGauge derives its centred glyph and value size from the box instead of the literals 11 and 8.

Seams: ccHome, ccResourceGroup, ccGaugeSize, paintRadialGauge, and TestControlCentreHomeSystemGaugesFitInsideCardBounds, whose (len(s)*8, 16) stub cannot see the current overflow.

Acceptance: docs/plans/assets/2026-09-17-metrics-control-centre-radial-design/acceptance-checklist.md

title: ccMonitor omits GPU and CPU temperature
description:
Found while designing the Home System card (2026-09-17). The Control Centre's own monitor section (ccMonitor in controlcenter_pages.go) builds graph cards for CPU, Memory and Network only. Once Home shows four metrics, that section contradicts the page one click away from it.

The standalone System Monitor (monitorTree) does carry GPU via selectGPU, and shows temperature as a second legend chip on the CPU card. So the gap is ccMonitor alone.

Needs a named decision: add GPU and temperature to ccMonitor, or state why the section is deliberately narrower. See design.md D4 in docs/plans/assets/2026-09-17-metrics-control-centre-radial-design/.

title: Radial thermal warning colour is nearly invisible
description:
Found while designing the Home System card (2026-09-17). radialWarningAmber applies theme.EnsureContrast(amber, track, 3), which walks #ffb300 toward black until it clears 3:1 against the track. The painted result is #6c4b00, a dark brown that reads as the arc fading out rather than as a warning on the dark card.

The error role above 85C receives no EnsureContrast treatment and sits at 1.20:1 against the track.

More broadly the arc is distinguished from the track by hue, not luminance: accent against track is 1.44:1.

The approved Home composition puts the number inside the ring, so the reading no longer depends on the arc. This issue is about whether the warning band should be legible as a warning at all. See design.md, Observations.

title: Settings input fields read as a thin bar at mini density
description: Reported by the owner from live use of the settings pane after M9 sub-project B. At mini density Metrics.InputHeight is 24, and a 24-pixel control reads as a thin bar rather than a field. Needs the owner's eye before the density ladder is touched: that metric is shared by every surface, so changing it moves controls everywhere. The control-sizing pass that stopped dropdowns and toggles stretching may have improved the proportion on its own, so re-look at the current build first.

title: Bar lane editor polish: insertion indicator, add-list filtering, group drag
description: The owner's verdict on the M9 sub-project B lane editor after live use: still rough. The tooltip, labelling and grouping-colour pass helped; it is not finished. Three concrete candidates, all on branch milestone/m9-bar-composition: (1) no insertion indicator when a drop would insert rather than join, so only the join target is marked; (2) the add list is 22 unfiltered rows and wants a filter; (3) a group's members cannot be reordered by drag, only by Alt+arrow.

title: M3: prevent a cancelled dwell callback showing a tooltip
description: A time.AfterFunc callback that has begun can outlive timer.Stop in dwell.leave, set shown after leave observed false, and send a show with no later hide. Add a generation/current-timer check under the mutex and a focused race-boundary test.

title: Clock and date pills paint empty for up to a minute after start
description: Observed on the laptop 2026-09-18 while running the sysc-321 live gate. After a systemctl restart the bar's clock and date pills render as empty rounded rects and stay empty until the next minute boundary, then fill in correctly. Reproduced on both the top and the lower edge, so it is not related to the bar anchor, and it reproduces on a binary built from main: pre-existing, not introduced by the bar geometry work. Likely the clock widget takes its first value from a minute-aligned tick rather than painting the current time at start.

title: Intel i915 GPU metrics integration and laptop qualification
description: Complete the M10 metrics, Control Centre, and GPU slice with the published sysc-metrics v0.5.1+ Intel i915 path. The shell metrics service must own one stateful GPUSampler, project the selected GPU consistently to the bar, System Monitor, and Control Centre, and retain exact-PCI GPU history. Record the laptop CAP_PERFMON requirement, the existing radial bar configuration, and the upstream completion evidence.
design: Use sysc-metrics GPUSampler as the only Intel reader. Keep sampler ownership in the shell metrics goroutine, keep GPU identity and history keyed by PCI ID, and leave unavailable usage truthful when PMU permission is absent. Do not add a shell-side perf reader or duplicate GPU sampler.
acceptance_criteria: Merge the feature implementation to main; keep the sysc-metrics v0.5.1+ pin; pass focused tests and the required shell gates; qualify Intel i915 usage on the laptop with the first sample as a baseline and the second sample valid; verify cap_perfmon on the installed binary and one live shell service; verify CPU, memory, temperature, and GPU radial bar entries; record the completion handover and README update.

The shell therefore dials a path nothing serves, checkSocket fails on Lstat, and no tray icon can ever paint. The package tests build the fake server's path from the same constant (client_test.go:23), so the suite stays green. Found while working docs/plans/2026-09-19-m9-overflow-and-tray-handover.md job one.

title: trayclient retries forever without reporting why it cannot reach the service

This is why sysc-411 survived in the field across two machines and several restarts - the handover records 'the shell logs no tray or presenter lines at all' as a symptom with no cause. Wants a reported first failure and a reported recovery, without a line per retry.

A damage-region publish would remove most of it. Measured 2026-09-19 at scale 1.25; bounded benchmark is 10.9ms at the Control Centre size after this tranche.

Per the Noctalia diffing model, a state change should retarget the existing width and fill transition channels on the same nodes, keeping identity stable, rather than replacing the row. Identity keys are already stable: each pill carries the compositor workspace id in its action.

title: Workspace pills: cycle workspaces on scroll

The bar already routes EventPointerAxis through an onAxis seam that resolves the action under the pointer, so the row needs an axis handler beside its action handler, plus a decision on whether the wheel wraps at the ends.

For the lower edge, shipped by sysc-321, the gap must sit at the surface's lower edge against the screen; the code instead floats it on the far side and runs the painted body flush to the screen edge. Derived from code during the sysc-804 investigation; not yet observed live. C2 must make the body derivation edge-aware anyway, so this fix belongs in that slice or immediately before it.

A live bar configured with four radial gauges came back with two radial and two text widgets. Media and clipboard had no branch either. Fixed by guarding on isMetric, the predicate the loader already used, plus a round-trip fixture per knownItems id so a new id cannot repeat it.

title: Shell motion: raise frame rate and cut per-frame paint cost
description: Measured on the laptop (eDP-1, 60.01Hz, 16.66ms budget): a full bar repaint costs 1.22ms with 1272 allocs, yet theme.BaseMotion.FrameCap=33ms paces every animating surface to ~30fps, exactly every other vblank. blendMask is 56.8% of the frame and reads its mask through image.Alpha.AlphaAt (Point.In + PixOffset per pixel); direct Pix indexing with an opaque fast path measured 5.0x faster and byte-identical. Animation is clocked by a free-running 16ms ticker rather than the frame callback the scheduler already owns, so frame spacing beats against vblank. Text is re-shaped through harfbuzz every repaint. Four parts: blendMask fast path, lower FrameCap, frame-callback-driven publishes, shaped-run cache.

title: Drive animation from the frame callback instead of a ticker
description: animateSurface samples unsettled values on a time.Ticker. The tick now runs at half a 60Hz frame so it cannot beat against the vblank, which removes the visible judder, but the sampling phase is still unrelated to the compositor's cadence: a value is read up to half a frame before it is presented. The architecturally correct form is to resample when wl_callback.done arrives, which the scheduler already receives (internal/render/schedule.go, done handler in internal/platform/wayland/client.go). That needs a seam from the Wayland owner back into the shell asking whether a surface is still unsettled, and that call would run on the owner goroutine and take a surface lock, so it needs care against the blank-shell failure mode. Deferred deliberately: the ticker change delivered most of the benefit at a fraction of the risk.

title: Weather bar element carried a redundant Weather label and only activated on left click

sysc-tray Proxy.Close self-deadlocks on the owner-left path
description: Terminate integration tests (sysc-tray redesign/v0.1, tests/integration/terminate_test.go) hang: when a real item owner process dies, the proxy pump detects owner-left and calls onItem -> dropWorker -> closeWorker -> Proxy.Close on the pump goroutine itself; Close blocks on <-p.looped/<-p.pumped, which only fire when pump returns. Self-deadlock. Existing tests never hit it because Close is only ever called from app.Close on a foreign goroutine. Fix direction: run the worker close off the pump goroutine (or make Close reentrancy-safe). Evidence: goroutine dump from go test ./tests/integration/ -run TestTerminate.

title: Stale gslapper socket files block wallpaper applies forever
description: A shell run killed without cleanup (observed Sep 16 08:42 on the desktop) leaves gslapper-<connector>.sock files in the runtime dir with no listener. Every later start, reconcile's Apply sees socket-exists + no owned process and correctly refuses (D17/D18), but there is no recovery path: launch refuses, stopOwned reports 'still holds', nothing unlinks a socket file that has no owner and no listener. Result: 'DP-x: wallpaper: DP-x socket is not owned by this shell' on every boot, wallpaper never applies, and because commit never happens the theme seed is never set. Fix direction: at Apply/launch, when the socket file exists but has no live peer (socketPeerPID fails or no listener), treat it as garbage and unlink before spawn — the same ownership proof socketFileIfOwned already uses, extended to the dead case.

title: Thumbnailer never publishes final counts when the walk tail has no new previews
description: Observed on the desktop: panel stuck at 'generating previews 228/645' while the walk had actually finished (642 cache hits + 3 webp decode errors; no ffmpeg running; last created attempt was index 227). generate() only calls note() when made=true, and the service publishes snapshots only on thumbProgress — so when every entry after the last creation is a cache hit, done reaches total but no final snapshot is ever published. The panel reads ThumbsDone/ThumbsTotal from the snapshot (service.go:482, popout_wallpaper.go:670) and shows a stale 'generating' state forever. Fix direction: publish once at the end of generate() regardless of made, or have the service publish when Counts() reports done==total after a progress tick.

title: Startup theme generation runs matugen with an empty seed and reports a scary failure every boot
description: Default ThemeGen is {Source: wallpaper, Seed: ""} because the seed is deliberately never persisted (D20: rebuilt from the wallpaper replay). At startup generateTheme therefore runs 'matugen image ""' which exits 1 ('No such file or directory', reproduced on matugen 4.2.0), the panel shows 'theme: matugen: exit status 1', and the compiled fallback paints. On a healthy boot the wallpaper apply then succeeds and notifySeed re-generates, so the error is transient noise — but when applies fail (see the stale-socket issue) it looks like a theme bug. Fix direction: skip the generator for an empty wallpaper seed the way Kind==palette already skips it, and surface 'waiting for first wallpaper' instead of a matugen failure.

title: plugin/v1 JSON encoder has no write mutex; concurrent Snapshot calls crash the plugin
description:
Framing encoder (plugin/v1/framing.go:71-106) has no write serialization. Any plugin whose publish() runs from more than one goroutine (poll tick + action goroutine is the common pattern — mini-docker does exactly this) can issue concurrent Snapshot calls while the main recv loop also writes, producing concurrent map/encoder writes and a crash that kills the pill.

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-{backend}-audit.md in sysc-plugins). The plugin currently must self-serialize around the whole client; that is an easy trap every plugin author will hit.
acceptance_criteria: Either the client serializes frame writes internally, or the plugin-v1 docs state the threading contract loudly; a regression test at the library level proves concurrent Snapshot is safe (or documented-unsafe with the contract spelled out).

title: Host silently rejects malformed plugin views (wrong root kind, node-budget overflow) with no signal
description:
When a plugin publishes a view the host cannot render, it is dropped with zero feedback to the plugin or logs: a tooltip published with a row root is silently rejected (host requires column roots for tooltips — mini-docker did exactly this and shipped a dead tooltip), and a tree exceeding the MaxNodes budget (1024) silently stops publishing (mini-docker would go blank past ~170 containers with docker ps -a).

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-{ui,ux}-audit.md in sysc-plugins). Both failures are invisible: the plugin author sees a blank panel and cannot tell why.
acceptance_criteria: Rejected publishes produce a diagnosable signal — at minimum a host-side log line naming plugin + view + reason; ideally a plugin-visible error response. Cover both the root-kind rule and the node-budget rule.

title: Document the plugin open-panel pattern (Button ID + CallPanelOpen) in plugin-v1 docs
description:
Panels only open when the plugin itself calls CallPanelOpen in response to a Button activate event with a chosen node ID (established pattern: timer main.go:85, world-clock). Nothing documents this, so a plugin whose bar is a bare text node ships an unopenable panel — mini-docker did exactly this and three independent audits initially attributed the blank panel elsewhere before converging on reachability.

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-ui-audit.md in sysc-plugins).
acceptance_criteria: plugin/v1 package docs (or the plugin authoring doc) state: panels open only via the plugin's own CallPanelOpen; show the minimal bar-button pattern; mention the tooltip column-root requirement in the same place.

Pass the service to the relay instead of re-reading the field. Pre-existing M4 (sysc-38) defect, not introduced by the sysc-41/42 work. title: Design user-managed plugin sources

sysc-wayland v0.2.0: unknown surface enter is fatal
description: REOPENED 2026-09-02: reproduced live on 715cc5f, not stale. 12 settings panel open/close cycles with the pointer over the panel produce 'dispatch: panic handling opcode=1 senderID=21: client: invalid server object ID 0x2b'. Battery icon font: all seven level glyphs are identical
description:
internal/render/icons/sysc-icons.ttf draws codepoints 0xE008 to 0xE00E (battery levels 0..6) as the same solid silhouette. Rendering the band at 96pt and at the bar's 17px shows no difference between an empty and a full battery.

BatteryIconRune is correct: 73 percent maps to level 5 of 0..6 and iconfont_test asserts every charge lands in the band. The selection works and the asset does not encode what was selected, so a battery widget cannot communicate charge through its icon. Live at 73 percent it reads as a solid block.

Fix belongs in the font asset: seven discharging and seven charging glyphs that actually differ, ideally an outline with a partial fill so the level reads at 17px. Check the critical glyph too. A test that rasterises each level and asserts the glyphs differ would stop this recurring, since the existing test only checks codepoint mapping.

title: Group members are not centred inside their capsule
description:
Live 2026-08-31: the grouped cpu and memory values sit off-centre inside the group pill.

Introduced by the group tranche. measureNode for KindRow now reports the tallest child rather than the band it was offered, so text measured at the physical size is not cropped. layoutCapsuleChild then grows the layout box to that height when it exceeds the capsule's inner band. Layout centres children against content.H of the grown box, not against the visible capsule, so members are pushed off centre.

Fix: centre members against the capsule's own inner band while still measuring them at their natural height. Add a test asserting a member's vertical centre matches the capsule's, with a child taller than the offered band.

title: Installed plugins built on an old SDK fail the handshake since host protocol floor 1.3

Since 5674306 (2026-09-20) the host offers only protocol 1.3-1.8 (internal/plugin/supervisor.go Supported), so a plugin binary built against an SDK whose ceiling is below 1.3 finds no common version and exits before replying. The laptop's previous build (2026-09-21) predated the floor. The desktop's weather plugin fails the same way on old and new builds. Either rebuild and reinstall the plugin binaries, or have the host log the version mismatch instead of EOF.

title: Stock themes are not selectable from settings
description: The design (D8, docs/plans/2026-08-30-settings-osd-theme-catalog-design.md) specifies ten curated seeds named as colour families, and selecting one sets theme source = stock plus that seed. internal/theme/stock.go carries all ten and theme.StockSeed resolves them, but the settings entry appearance.seed is KindString with no Options, so a user has to type the exact name. theme.StockNames has no caller outside tests. Make appearance.seed offer StockNames when appearance.source is stock, which needs an entry whose options depend on another entry's value; the settings registry has no such dependency today.
notes: Verified against A's design 2026-09-17: NOT automatically fixed by it. docs/plans/2026-09-15-settings-foundation-design.md gives each entry typed get/set closures, but says nothing about options that depend on another entry's value, which is precisely what this bug needs. settings.DefaultFor(cfg) already builds entries from a config, so the capability is within reach, but PanelHost.set is constructed once when the panel opens. Under A's live-apply a change to appearance.source would therefore not refresh appearance.seed's options. A needs either a registry rebuild from the draft after each change, or Options as a closure over config. Fold into sysc-330 rather than treating this as separately fixed.
