title: sysc-metrics: GPU usage for xe from drm-cycles fdinfo
description: v0.7.0's fdinfo fallback reads drm-engine-<class> ns (i915, amdgpu). xe publishes drm-cycles-<class> and drm-total-cycles-<class>, so xe GPUs (Lunar Lake and later, and i915 parts opted into xe) still report no usage. Busy per class = sum over clients of delta cycles / delta total-cycles, divided by capacity. Needs xe hardware to prove live.

title: sysc-metrics: GPU sample repeats pci.ids lookup and denied PMU opens every second
description: On the UHD 620 laptop one GPUSampler.Sample takes ~34 ms: ~10 ms is ReadGPU's pci.ids name lookup, repeated each sample for a name that never changes, and the rest includes four perf_event_open calls that are denied every sample, plus the 7 ms fdinfo walk. Cache names per PCI ID and stop reopening a PMU counter after EACCES/EPERM (retry rarely). Measure before and after.

title: Narrow the dead-socket probe-then-remove window in wallpaper Apply
description: Review finding: Apply probes deadSocketFile then os.Remove; a foreign process could unlink the dead file and bind a live socket in the window, and the remove would then unlink a live foreign socket. deadSocketFile could return the FileInfo and the unlink could route through removeSocketIfSame (inode compare). Residual race is inherent to probe-then-unlink; defense-in-depth, not a correctness fix.

title: Pin stopOwned's refusal of a live foreign socket with a test
description: Review finding: stopOwned's no-process branch unlinks a provably dead socket but has no test that it still refuses a socket with a live listener; Apply's equivalent guard is tested (TestEngineStillRefusesForeignLiveSocket). Add the stopOwned-side test.

title: Plugin panels: report the granted size in view.open and find the laptop width clamp
description:
On the laptop (eDP-1, 1536x864 logical, scale 1.25) the calendar panel (manifest 1040x760) is drawn about 810x758: width clamped, height intact. Placement.FittedSize would allow ~1500 wide, so something else clamps width. Separately, pluginHost.openPanel (internal/shell/pluginhost.go ~806-834) fills view.open Width/Height from the manifest (spec.Width/Height), so a plugin is told 1040x760 while its tree is laid out in the smaller surface: plugins cannot lay out for the box they actually get, and layout the plugin linted at the declared size can be refused (calendar's status-banner Refresh button fails lint at 810x758).

Wanted: (1) root-cause the width clamp; (2) view.open (and a resize path when the surface changes) carries the fitted/granted size; (3) test that a panel declared wider than its placement is told the smaller size.

Consumer: sysc-plugins calendar (currently designed for a fixed 800x720 as a workaround, see sysc-plugins docs/plans/2026-09-25-world-clock-handover.md and the calendar polish commit). Evidence: laptop screenshots 2026-09-26, panel borders at x=905..1918 physical.

title: Icon advance is narrower than its ink

Widening the advance to 1260 corrupted the whole bar rather than only the spacing, which suggests the mask or blend path does not handle an advance wider than the em, or that the corruption has a different cause entirely. See the corrupt-render issue. Fix the spacing once rendering is trustworthy again.

title: Apply's stale-socket error double-prefixes wallpaper:
description: Review nit from sysc-576: Apply wraps removeSocketIfSame's error with 'wallpaper: clear stale %s socket: %w', but removeSocketIfSame already returns 'wallpaper: socket path %s changed while it was stopped', yielding 'wallpaper: clear stale DP-1 socket: wallpaper: socket path ... changed...'. Cosmetic; the wrap is still needed for raw os.Remove errors. Clean fix is to strip the prefix from removeSocketIfSame's errors and wrap at each call site (Apply, stopOwned no-process, stopOwned owned-process paths), which touches the stopOwned error contract.

title: TestEngineDoesNotRemoveReplacedSocket is inode-reuse flaky on ext4
description: The test removed the socket then wrote a replacement at the same path; on ext4 the replacement reuses the freed inode, os.SameFile is true, stopOwned sends stop, the fake peer removes the file, removeSocketIfSame sees it vanished and returns nil, so Restore reports success and the test fails. Passes on tmpfs where inodes are not reused. Pre-existing on main; exposed by the full-repo -race gate with TMPDIR on ext4.

title: bd export drops issue comments from the tracked JSONL
description: The CLI bd export (cmd/bd/export.go in steveyegge/beads 0.17.7) populates dependencies and labels but never populates issue.Comments, so every CLI export rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl without the comments that the daemon/RPC auto-export path (internal/rpc/server_export_import_auto.go) includes. The AGENTS.md recovery procedure (DELETE FROM export_hashes; bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl) therefore silently drops comments from the tracked file; the DB keeps them (comments table intact). Observed 2026-09-27: 17 comment-bearing lines in HEAD, 0 after recovery, 22 rows still in the comments table. Guard: after any CLI export, grep -c '"comments"' .beads/issues.jsonl and restore from git if it dropped.

title: sysc-plugins CI red: go vet fails on runner (calendar libecal-2.0) + TestPluginCalendarGateAllViews broken by 2f1961f
description:
Two independent pre-existing failures on sysc-plugins main (found while fixing sysc-519; NOT mini-docker).

1) CI's actual first failure is 'go vet ./...' (37-43s then exit 1): plugins/calendar requires cgo libecal-2.0 (EDS), not installed on the GitHub runner: 'Package libecal-2.0 was not found in the pkg-config search path'. This masks every later CI step. Evidence: gh run view 36249418113 --log-failed; recent main runs all fail this way (36249418113, 36247382564, 36233161307, 36161564656, 36158589304). Options: install EDS in CI, build-tag the cgo file, or make vet skip calendar.

2) TestPluginCalendarGateAllViews fails deterministically on a clean tree, with and without -race (~5.6s = 5s waitNode deadline). Root cause: panelTitle() at tests/integration/plugin_calendar_gate_test.go:166-171 returns root.Children[0].Children[1].Text, but the current calendar header row's Children[1] is the cal-shortcuts icon button (no Text); the title text ('September 2026') now lives at root.Children[0].Children[0].Children[1]. Introduced by commit 2f1961f 'fix(calendar): design the panel for the box every screen grants'. Fix: one-line panelTitle path change (or search for the title text node).

Note: plugins/screen-recorder TestRecorderRepeatedToggleDoesNotRestart flaked once in a parallel full-suite run ('mode = recording, want idle', recorder_test.go:77), passed on rerun (7.657s) - timing flake, not investigated.

Drain repaint requests before the Wayland startup handshake
description: Laptop deployment hung during startup. The captured stack shows the Wayland owner blocked in SetCapabilities -> publishSurface during connect(). The eight-entry invalidation channel was full; wake.bridge only started later in loop(). Notification handling then blocked on the same queue while holding Registry.mu, so IPC also timed out. Start the existing bridge before connect and join it before closing its pipe.
acceptance_criteria: A full repaint queue drains while a test compositor holds the initial handshake open. Connection failure cleans up the bridge. Race checks pass and the laptop renders its bar and answers IPC after deployment.
notes:
Confirmed startup deadlock during laptop deployment of sysc-820 revision e0c6255. Captured stack: Registry.SetCapabilities -> publishSurface blocks during the second Wayland connection roundtrip because the eight-entry invalidation queue is full. Its reader starts only after connect returns. A notification publisher also blocks while holding Registry.mu, causing IPC timeouts. This startup ordering predates sysc-820.

Evidence: /tmp/sysc590-goroutines.txt. Recovered laptop archThink with saved revision 278deeb322c516c9c1e378a8fdee077c6e0aefac through the deployment installer. IPC responded and screenshot /tmp/sysc590-restored.png showed the bar.

Fix: start the existing wake bridge before connect, then cancel and join it before closing the wake pipe. Regression test fills the queue during a held initial handshake, verifies publication continues, and checks Run exits on disconnect.

Verification: on main 8225083, gofmt, GOMAXPROCS=4 go vet -p 2 ./..., and the full internal/platform/wayland race tests pass. Race tests ran serially by package because the machine guard blocks repo-wide race builds after prior hard locks. A package-by-package race run on 08449de passed all but internal/shell (section validation and battery layout expectations) and tests/integration (tray hit targets); those failures reproduce in the affected tests on 8225083 and do not call Wayland Run.

Live laptop proof: deployed commit 38dfae739a8a through scripts/deploy. On archThink, sysc-shell ipc status returned ok=true, Niri listed sysc-shell:bar on eDP-1, and /tmp/sysc668-fixed-bar.png shows the rendered bar.

title: Registry audio/brightness OSD relay races with service swap
description:
go test -race ./internal/shell fails on main at 2c2fb7e (~20 tests in one package; the non-race run is clean).

Root cause: Registry.setAudio writes r.audio then launches 'go r.relayAudioOSD()', and the goroutine reads r.audio with no synchronisation. A second setAudio (service reload, or a test that swaps the service) writes the field while a live relay goroutine reads it. registry.go:102 (write) vs registry.go:271 (read). setBrightness has the same shape.

Found during Milestone 6A Task 0 reconciliation. Pre-existing, not caused by M6. Recorded rather than fixed because Registry is being changed by the in-flight M5 work.

Fix direction: pass the service to relayAudioOSD as an argument, or guard the field under the existing Registry mutex, and give the relay goroutine a per-generation stop signal so an old relay cannot outlive its service.

title: Icon resolver drops 37% of application icons: no SVG support
description:
internal/icons is raster-only by design (package doc: 'Milestone 5 is raster-only. No SVG rasterizer is pinned'). Measured against the desktop's real 199 launcher entries through the resolver the launcher actually uses:

  74 of 199 (37%) fail to resolve and fall back to the letter capsule
  66 of those 74 have an SVG on disk that would have resolved
   6 have nothing on disk

title: Panel backdrop blur: screencopy binding and blur kernel
description:
Executes docs/plans/2026-09-11-panel-backdrop-blur.md Tasks 1-10 on feature/panel-backdrop-blur, rebased onto main at 79e9899 (which brought the control-centre work in). Eleven commits.

Measured 2026-09-12/13 (go1.27.0, Ryzen 7 5700X, powersave): blur kernel 4.94 ms median against a predicted 4.60, linear at 4.6-5.1 ms/MPix over six panel sizes; screencopy readback 5.67 ms median against D16.1's 15 ms stop threshold; ~11 ms per open, inside one 60 Hz frame.

Design corrections found live, each by measurement rather than reading: this Niri offers xrgb8888 only for a region capture, so the captured alpha byte must be filled; a screencopy target's wl_shm pool must hold exactly one buffer, which newGeneration cannot do (hence newCaptureBuffer); the backdrop must go through the rounded mask or panel corners fill in; the shell, not the wayland package, assembles a panel's Style, so the image returns via a new HostCallbacks.Backdrop; and the panel-opacity bound had to move in three places or the lower floor stayed unreachable from config.

capture_output_region is OUTPUT-RELATIVE, not global: probed directly because this output sits at logical 2560,0. A global-space region is refused with nil, an output-relative one returns real content. D3 assumed this and never verified it.

Post-rebase defect found and fixed (876ca72): main's AttachedPanelStyle resolves an attached panel's root at the BAR's opacity, which is opaque, so an attached panel painted straight over its own backdrop. Caught by measuring a live capture: the Audio panel body was a single flat colour, pixel-identical to the bar fill. rootStyle now keeps the panel's own alpha whenever a backdrop is present, with a regression test.

Verified live on two machines: archPC 3440x1440 scale 1.0 and archThink 1920x1080 scale 1.25 (the first fractional-scale exercise of this path). Blur visible on both; ships off by default.

Depends on (1):
  → sysc-202: Milestone 8: rendering qualification [P2]

Coverage gate added 2026-09-13 (9537440): blur is enforced for panels that do not exist yet, not merely true for today's. internal/shell/blurcoverage_test.go walks the whole PanelID enum (failing if it grows past the known end) and scans package sources so every wayland.AuxSpec either sets BlurRegion or carries a blur-exempt comment with its reason. Seven surfaces carry reasons; three of them - the running-apps menu, the tray menu and the tray drawer - record an open scope question for the owner rather than a settled no, because design D13 names neither.

title: Weather surfaces are unstyled and under-informed: audit and parity pass
description:
Audit 2026-09-15 of every first-party weather presentation against the DMS/Noctalia v4 reference (docs/plans/assets/2026-08-31-bar-visual-parity/refs/noctalia-weather.png).

Presentations today, three sites, all thin:

- Bar widget (widget.go:226, weatherwidget.go): one text run - inline WMO glyph + temperature + optional condition word + stale age. The glyph is text, not an icon node: it inherits text tone and metrics, so sysc-58's advance defect applies to it. The tooltip is the static word "Weather" (textWidget.tooltip is a plain string). No Action is set: clicking does nothing.
- Control centre weather page (controlcenter_pages.go:349 ccWeather): a Today card that presents raw coordinates ("%.2f deg, %.2f deg") as the location plus "Updated 15:04"; below it four 143x132 forecast cards showing day name, glyph and "H / L" only - no condition word, today excluded, count pinned at four.
- No standalone weather panel exists.

Data path (weather/client.go, weather/model.go, internal/services/weather.go): the request carries current=temperature_2m,weather_code and daily=weather_code,max,min,sunrise,sunset for seven days. Open-Meteo also returns, and Decode silently discards, elevation and timezone from the response root; the current block can carry is_day, apparent_temperature, humidity, wind_speed_10m, wind_direction_10m and uv_index; the daily block can carry uv_index_max and precipitation figures. The reference panel shows wind, UV, elevation and a named timezone; none of that is reachable today without extending the wire model.

Vocabulary drift - three copies of the same facts:

- Icon mapping: render/iconfont.go IconRune/IconName (eight WMO glyphs) versus ccWeatherIcon's separate Material ligature set (sunny, partly_cloudy_day, ...) for the same codes.
- Condition words: conditionWords (weatherwidget.go:14), ccWeatherCondition, and the plugin's Condition() are three tables. The plugin's routes through IconName; the shell's two do not agree with each other.
- No night variants: WMO code 0 at night renders a sun; is_day is not fetched.

State handling drift: formatWeather's three-state rule (placeholder / error / stale-with-age) lives in the bar only. ccWeather dashes and "Updated HH:MM" ignore FailedSince, so an aged reading renders identically to a fresh one.

Conformance and collision hazards: ccWeather's geometry (Height 336/480, 132; Width 143; Gap 8/12) sits on the open token-conformance worklist, and the parked feature/noctalia-parity session has controlcenter_pages.go dirty in its worktree. This slice must not re-edit that page's geometry concurrently - sequence the cc page after parity lands or confine this slice to new files.
acceptance_criteria:
- weather.Query/Forecast/Decode extended for current is_day, apparent_temperature, wind speed and direction, humidity, uv_index; daily uv_index_max and precipitation; root elevation, timezone, timezone_abbreviation. Decode stays strict: checked pointer fields, bounded body, table tests for the new fields.
- One icon mapping and one condition-word table shared by the bar, the control-centre page and the tooltip; night variants for clear and partly-cloudy added to the icon subset and selected via is_day.
- The bar weather widget renders a real icon node beside the temperature, opens the weather panel as its Action, and its tooltip carries current facts rather than the literal word "Weather".
- A standalone PanelWeather appended to the PanelID enum after PanelNetwork (the blur coverage walk must see it), composed like the reference: hero card (large glyph, temperature, min/max, condition, configured location name - not coordinates), a details card (feels-like, wind, humidity, UV, sunrise, sunset, elevation, timezone), and the seven-day list with per-day icon, day, range and condition word. Daily only; Hourly is a separate decision with its own wire growth.
- Stale and error states follow formatWeather's three-state rule on every surface; an aged reading looks aged everywhere.
- No new literal geometry: spacing from the margin ladder, control sizes from the density row, shapes from the shape role. The control-centre page's existing literals stay untouched until the parity conversion lands.
- Focused checks per changed unit; gofmt, go vet, and the affected-package gates pass before any commit.
notes:
Scope note 2026-09-15: the parity slices ran on feature/weather-panel and were audited together. The hourly presentation is intentionally capped at seven rows to match the reference; the panel remains two-column per the recorded amendment; the city-only unresolved fallback retains the configured city label rather than fabricating zero coordinates.

Audit verdict 2026-09-16: merge-ready with named corrections applied. Closed findings: sysc-295 (nullable decode and optional-row padding), sysc-296 (control-centre night/stale/error state), sysc-297 (hourly row cap), sysc-298 (detail order), sysc-299 (unresolved-city label), sysc-300 (date-stable fixtures), sysc-301 (Fahrenheit range units), sysc-302 (in-flight city-change cache race). Completed parity slices sysc-287, sysc-288 and sysc-294 are closed.

Proof: GOMAXPROCS=4 go test -p 2 ./weather/ ./internal/services/ ./internal/render/ ./internal/config/ ./internal/theme/ ./internal/shell/ ./internal/plugin/ ./tests/... -count=1; GOMAXPROCS=4 go build -p 2 ./...; GOMAXPROCS=4 go vet -p 2 ./...; gofmt scan; git diff --check; legacy-visual and backdrop scans; night/detail font-ink tests; go.mod/go.sum diff clean.

The owner-gated live Niri check remains outstanding; do not deploy or restart the service from this audit.

title: Launcher follow-up: windows/Niri-focus provider
GPU metrics stop publishing after working
description: GPU metrics can stop publishing entirely after previously working. On 2026-09-22 the desktop still exposes NVIDIA PCI 0000:08:00.0 through /sys/class/drm, but nvidia-smi fails to communicate with the driver; kernel logs show NVIDIA GPU out-of-memory failures on 2026-09-21 16:39 +10. Reproduce and instrument the seam from the shell SourceGPU lease through GPUSampler.Sample, snapshot/update delivery, exact PCI history, and bar/Control Centre projection. Record whether sampling errors, leases stop, updates stop, or projection drops values; preserve truthful unavailable state and do not add a shell-side nvidia-smi reader. Acceptance: a focused regression check identifies the failing seam, live evidence captures recovery or a bounded diagnosis, and the M10 GPU path remains single-sampler and exact-PCI keyed.

title: plugin/v1 JSON encoder has no write mutex; concurrent Snapshot calls crash the plugin
description:
Framing encoder (plugin/v1/framing.go:71-106) has no write serialization. Any plugin whose publish() runs from more than one goroutine (poll tick + action goroutine is the common pattern — mini-docker does exactly this) can issue concurrent Snapshot calls while the main recv loop also writes, producing concurrent map/encoder writes and a crash that kills the pill.

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-{backend}-audit.md in sysc-plugins). The plugin currently must self-serialize around the whole client; that is an easy trap every plugin author will hit.
acceptance_criteria: Either the client serializes frame writes internally, or the plugin-v1 docs state the threading contract loudly; a regression test at the library level proves concurrent Snapshot is safe (or documented-unsafe with the contract spelled out).

comments.text:
Tasks 9-11 done on milestone/launcher (worktree clean, full suite + -race + vet green, 15 commits total).

T9 activation: Service.Activate(id, action) -> niri msg action spawn -- argv on the query worker, bounded 5s ctx, injectable runner; usage recorded on success only, keyed by the routed provider query. Missing niri = error, not panic.

T10 panel: PanelLauncher registered (parsePanelName/panelIDFromAux/String), 560x500, Placement.CenterY floats it centered in output minus bar zone + padding. Rows non-focusable so the field keeps focus; arrows clamp selection with scroll ensure-visible; Enter activates (overview prefix rows navigate into the provider); right-click opens actions KindMenu; Esc closes; spawn async off the Wayland goroutine, failure shows error label and keeps panel open. Service created lazily on first launcher open (keeps idle registries from paying the XDG scan); relay goroutine pumps Results into the open panel.
